newsitem.title: JAPAN: Official says Russia may join nuclear dumping ban.
newsitem.headline: Official says Russia may join nuclear dumping ban.

text.p: Russia's Nuclear Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov said on Tuesday that Moscow was likely to join a global ban later this year on the dumping of nuclear waste at sea.

"I believe we will accept (the ban) by the end of this year," a Japanese government official quoted Mikhailov as telling Japanese Science and Technology Agency chief Riichiro Chikaoka at a meeting in Tokyo.
The ban on dumping low- and intermediate-level radioactive waste was agreed in November 1993 at the London Convention, which deals with global ocean issues.
Russia abstained from voting on the ban, arguing that it could not end nuclear dumping until it had built a land disposal site, preferably with foreign aid.
Russia dumped some 900 tonnes of low-level liquid nuclear waste in the Sea of Japan in October 1993, sparking an outcry in Japan, South Korea and the United States.
The ban was to be reviewed internationally in 25 years.
Mikhailov also urged Japan to buy enriched uranium removed from Russia's dismantled missiles, the Japanese official said.
